From this he draws his real point: people disagree not because some have more reason, but because they use it differently. That sets up the need for a method. Readers have long noted a possible irony in the opening, since the evidence offered is that no one wants more good sense, which may show only that everyone overrates their own.
interpretation.zh: 笛卡尔以这样的观察开启《谈谈方法》：人人似乎都满足于自己那份良知，他把这看作判断是非的能力人人相等的迹象。由此他引出真正的论点：人们意见不同，不是因为有人理性更多，而是因为运用理性的方式不同，这就引出了对方法的需要。读者早已注意到开头可能带有反讽，因为他给出的证据是没人想要更多良知，而这或许只说明人人都高估了自己。

entries.name: Rene Descartes
entries.en: …to divide each of the difficulties under examination into as many parts as possible, and as might be necessary for its adequate solution.
entries.work: Discourse on the Method of Rightly Conducting One's Reason and of Seeking Truth in the Sciences
entries.context: Discourse on Method, Part II: the second of the four rules Descartes set himself.

interpretation.en: Descartes is setting out the four rules he chose in place of the many precepts of traditional logic, comparing himself to a state that governs best with few laws strictly kept. This second rule tells him to break any problem into as many smaller parts as needed to solve it. It follows the first rule, to accept nothing as true unless it is clear beyond doubt, and the idea is that small parts can each be seen clearly where the whole problem cannot.
interpretation.zh: 笛卡尔在列出他用来替代传统逻辑繁多规则的四条准则，并把自己比作一个法律少而执行严格、因而治理得最好的国家。这第二条准则要求把任何难题分成尽可能多、足以解决它的小部分。它承接第一条准则，即凡未清楚到无可怀疑的，都不当作真；其想法是，整体难以看清时，各个小部分却可以分别看清。

entries.name: Aristotle
entries.en: …it is not one swallow or one fine day that makes a spring, so it is not one day or a short time that makes a man blessed and happy.
entries.work: The Nicomachean Ethics
entries.context: The Nicomachean Ethics, Book I, chapter 7: happiness belongs to a whole life, not a single day.

interpretation.en: This closes Aristotle's definition of happiness as activity of the soul in accordance with virtue, to which he adds that it must be over a complete life. The swallow image makes the point that one good stretch does not make a person happy, because happiness is a quality of a whole life rather than a passing state. He then calls the definition only a rough outline to be filled in later, and the question of how misfortune late in life affects happiness returns in Book I.
interpretation.zh: 这句话结束了亚里士多德对幸福的定义：幸福是灵魂合乎德性的活动，他又补充说，这必须贯穿完整的一生。燕子的比喻说明，一段美好的时光并不能使人幸福，因为幸福是整个一生的品质，而非一时的状态。随后他称这个定义只是一个粗略的轮廓，有待日后充实；晚年的不幸如何影响幸福的问题，在第一卷后面还会再次出现。

entries.name: George Berkeley
entries.en: …we have first raised a dust and then complain we cannot see.
entries.work: A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge
entries.context: Berkeley's introduction to A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge, on difficulties philosophers make for themselves.

interpretation.en: In the introduction to the Principles Berkeley rejects the idea that philosophical puzzles show human faculties are too weak to know the truth. He argues that God would not give people a strong desire for knowledge and then put it out of reach, so the fault lies in how the faculties are used. The image of raising dust captures his diagnosis: most philosophical difficulties are self-made, and he goes on to blame chiefly the doctrine of abstract ideas.
interpretation.zh: 在《人类知识原理》的导论中，贝克莱反对这样一种看法：哲学难题表明人的能力太弱，无法认识真理。他认为，上帝不会给人强烈的求知欲，又让知识遥不可及，所以问题出在对这些能力的使用上。扬起尘土的比喻概括了他的诊断：大多数哲学困难是自己造成的，他接着把主要责任归于抽象观念的学说。

entries.name: George Berkeley
entries.en: Few men think; yet all have opinions.
entries.work: Three Dialogues Between Hylas and Philonous
entries.context: Three Dialogues between Hylas and Philonous; Philonous, Berkeley's spokesman, answers Hylas.

interpretation.en: This is said by Philonous, Berkeley's spokesman, after Hylas suggests his view is close to Malebranche's claim that all things are seen in God. Philonous answers that people who form opinions without thinking tend to confuse quite different doctrines. He then sets out how his position differs: Malebranche relies on abstract general ideas and an absolute external world, both of which Berkeley rejects.
interpretation.zh: 这句话出自贝克莱的代言人斐洛诺斯之口，当时海拉斯暗示他的观点接近马勒伯朗士所说的在上帝之中看见万物。斐洛诺斯回答说，不加思考便形成意见的人，往往会把截然不同的学说混为一谈。随后他说明自己的立场与之有何不同：马勒伯朗士依赖抽象的一般观念和绝对的外部世界，而贝克莱两者都否定。

entries.name: Ralph Waldo Emerson
entries.en: Nothing can bring you peace but yourself.
entries.work: Essays: First Series
entries.context: The second-to-last line of Emerson's essay "Self-Reliance", warning against trusting good luck for peace of mind.

interpretation.en: This is the second-to-last sentence of Self-Reliance. Emerson has just described how a turn of good fortune lifts people's spirits and makes them expect good days, and he dismisses that hope. Peace, he says, cannot come from outside events at all, only from the self, and the essay's final sentence restates this as the triumph of principles. The two lines together sum up the essay's argument that reliance on externals, whether custom, opinion or luck, is the opposite of self-reliance.
interpretation.zh: 这是《自立》的倒数第二句。爱默生刚刚描述了好运如何让人精神振奋、期待好日子，并否定了这种期望。他说，平静根本不可能来自外在事件，只能来自自身；文章最后一句又把这一点重申为原则的胜利。两句合起来概括了全文的论点：依赖外物，无论是习俗、舆论还是运气，都与自立背道而驰。
